mint.note: capture_start_state.py's --game whitelist does not include this title; ran it with an arbitrary --game label plus explicit --rom/--out (the script only uses --game for the DEFAULT_ROMS lookup, which is skipped when --rom is passed). is_controllable() (growth + directionality over RIGHT/LEFT holds) fired at frame 315 on the first try, no manual menu navigation needed. Copied to the canonical roms/ sidecar path after landing.

odometer_gate.finding: INSTRUMENT BUG, not a game finding. The default Pool (disable_asm_cpu=False, nes_core/src/nes.rs) produced a completely flat odometer (range x=0,y=4, oam_churn=1/1199) IDENTICALLY for right/left/up/down/A -- five different held inputs converging on the exact same trace is the signature of the ASM-CPU PPU/NMI-batching bug already on record in project memory for SMB ('ASM CPU disabled -- Mario walks'; interpreter path is byte-exact). Verified directly against nes_core.NESEnvironment (which has no ASM-CPU toggle and always runs the interpreter) holding RIGHT for 1500 frames: real scroll growth to odo_x=783 by frame ~800, screenshots showing live gameplay (health bar, player sprite, two flanking enemies, scrolling city skyline) confirmed visually. Re-ran the gate with pool.set_disable_asm_cpu(True) patched in post-construction (same slot go_explore_solve.py's apply_hw_flags uses, before reset_all): range_x=783, axis=x, distinct=137, oam_churn=842/1199 (agent clearly alive/animating), tail flat (behaviour finding: plateaus under a naive constant-RIGHT hold, expected for a run-and-gun with jump-required obstacles). No script files were edited -- the workaround was applied by monkeypatching within a throwaway driver script, not the repo's go_explore_solve.py/progress_signal_gate.py.
odometer_gate.verdict: REAL SCROLL AXIS CONFIRMED (once the ASM-CPU instrument bug is worked around).

smoke.note: Frontier is NOT stuck at 1 and never stalled -- cell count nearly doubled between the two 60s checkpoints (789 -> 1481) with frontier still wide open (1217 of 1481 cells) at the end. best_score/max_gx_in_max_area climbed 1249 -> 2030 across the same window, well past the 783 plateau the naive constant-RIGHT gate hit -- confirms the richer action set (jump/shoot combos) gets past the obstacle a hold-right driver alone cannot. 0 solutions in budget is expected (level_key is the empty coverage baseline, same as every other wave's smoke).

classification_rationale: Real scroll axis confirmed once a default-Pool ASM-CPU instrument bug (verified against the interpreter-path NESEnvironment and visually against rendered frames) was worked around; the 2-minute/4-worker smoke run under the same workaround grew from 1 to 1481 cells with 1217 still on the open frontier and best_score still climbing at the 2-minute mark -- unambiguously not the SOUND_GAME_STOPS freeze pattern.
next_lever: The ASM-CPU default bug is a real, generic instrument defect (not a Journey to Silius-specific hack) -- same bug class already on record for SMB. Worth checking whether other onboarded titles are silently affected the same way (a flat/near-flat odometer gate that was accepted as CAMERA_STATIC_AGENT_ACTIVE without cross-checking against the interpreter path could be misdiagnosed). A permanent fix belongs in go_explore_solve.py's Pool construction / apply_hw_flags path (exposing disable_asm_cpu as a resolvable flag) rather than a per-run monkeypatch, but that change was left out of scope for this single-game onboarding task.
wall_clock_budget: workers capped at 4, smoke capped at 2 minutes per task instructions; total wall-clock for this game ran well over the ~8-minute target because of the ASM-CPU instrument-bug diagnosis (root-caused and workaround-verified against ground truth, not left as an unexplained freeze).
